note: Each record is the FULL reasoning path an agent took: problem -> evidence -> hypotheses -> decision procedure -> solution -> verification -> generalization. This is the training signal: the thought process, not the diff.

problem: File fails to compile: 'try:' at line 95 with no except
evidence: py_compile reported SyntaxError: expected 'except' or 'finally' block
line 92: 'try: import arms.support_arms' followed by another 'try: import arms.kali_arm'
grep showed the identical broken pattern repeated 5x in the same file
hypotheses: 1. Single typo in one block
2. Copy-paste scaffolding bug propagated through multiple import blocks
decision_procedure: Count occurrences before editing (5 found) -> fix pattern must be applied everywhere, not once -> verify with py_compile after
solution: Each bare try got its own except Exception: pass; each over-nested try got its except
generalization: When pyflakes/py_compile reports a pattern error, ALWAYS grep for the same pattern elsewhere in the file before fixing — repeated blocks propagate the same bug. apply with allowMultiple after confirming count.

problem: NameError risk: name referenced in code but not imported
evidence: pyflakes: undefined name X
grep of import block shows the import was removed or renamed (e.g., 'import sys as _sys')
hypotheses: 1. Import genuinely missing
2. Import aliased/renamed elsewhere (sys vs _sys)
3. Imported conditionally inside a branch that doesn't always run
decision_procedure: grep the module's full import block -> if an alias exists, use it (minimal diff); if not, add the canonical import at module top, not inside functions
solution: Used _sys.executable where sys was aliased; added missing imports at module top elsewhere
generalization: Refactors that alias imports (import sys as _sys) silently break every later reference to the old name. After any import rename, grep the whole module for the old name. Prefer module-top imports; function-local imports are only safe for names used inside that function's body, never in annotations or other functions.

problem: pyflakes: undefined name Path/argparse even though 'from pathlib import Path' appears in the file
evidence: grep shows the import INSIDE the module docstring (line 4, between """ delimiters)
pattern found in 11 files including all 8 make_video* templates
hypotheses: 1. Import shadowed by a later one
2. Import text is dead — inside docstring, never executed
decision_procedure: Check line position relative to docstring open/close -> if between them, it is dead text -> find where the docstring closes and re-insert after it
solution: Moved the import out of the docstring to module level (removed from inside, inserted after closing """)
generalization: Docstrings grow over imports during documentation edits. This is a HIGH-frequency corruption (11/38 fixes). When pyflakes says a name is undefined but grep finds the import, ALWAYS check whether the import line sits between """ delimiters. Template files propagate the same defect to all variants.

problem: pyflakes: np undefined in '-> dict[str, np.ndarray]' annotation and in function body
evidence: grep shows 'import numpy as np' exists but INSIDE the function's try block
annotations are evaluated at function/class DEFINITION time, before the body runs
hypotheses: 1. Module-level import missing
2. Import exists but too late (function-local) for annotation evaluation
decision_procedure: Locate where np is first used -> if first use is an annotation, the import MUST be module-level -> move/add module-level guarded import
solution: Added module-level 'import numpy as np' with try/except ImportError fallback (np = None)
generalization: Type annotations execute at definition time. A function-local import is invisible to annotations on that same function. Rule: any name appearing in an annotation needs a module-level import (or from __future__ import annotations).

problem: pyflakes: frame_num undefined at line 680 of a script that builds a generated .py file via f-string
evidence: line 680 is inside create_script = f''' ... '''
other interpolations in the same f-string are escaped as {{var}} but this one is not
the escaped ones emit literal {var} for the GENERATED script's own loop variables
hypotheses: 1. frame_num should exist in outer scope (missing variable)
2. frame_num is a variable of the GENERATED script and must be escaped {{}} so it stays literal
decision_procedure: Identify what the f-string is for (generated script vs direct code) -> check sibling interpolations: are loop vars escaped? if yes, this one is a missed escape, not a missing var
solution: Changed {frame_num:06d} to {{frame_num:06d}} so the generated script receives literal {frame_num:06d}
verification: pyflakes clean; AST shows no unescaped interpolations of undefined names
generalization: In f-strings that generate code, every literal brace must be doubled. When you see undefined-name warnings inside an f-string, check whether the file is a code GENERATOR — if so, the fix is escaping, not importing.

problem: pyflakes: _draw_glow() called at line 655 but never defined
evidence: grep 'def _draw_glow' returns nothing
call site passes (draw, cx, cy, radius, color, alpha) — 6 args
sibling helpers _blend_color, _find_theme exist nearby
hypotheses: 1. Helper was deleted
2. Helper renamed
3. Helper never written (reference added before implementation)
decision_procedure: grep for any def variant -> none -> the helper must be created -> infer signature from the call site and the visual intent (radial glow behind badges)
solution: Implemented _draw_glow(draw, cx, cy, radius, color, alpha) drawing concentric fading ellipses
verification: pyflakes clean; signature matches call site
generalization: When a function is called but undefined, the call site IS the spec: argument order and names reveal the intended signature. Implement minimally to satisfy the call, matching sibling helpers' style.

problem: pyflakes: ConsistencyChecker undefined; file compiles but all methods nested inside each other with hundreds of spaces
evidence: grep of top-level defs shows everything indented under one class
main/process_directory unreachable
same class in generate_docstrings.py (4 functions nested in 1)
hypotheses: 1. File corrupted by bad auto-edit
2. File was always broken (generated by a tool that mis-indented)
decision_procedure: Check if the module is imported/referenced anywhere (orphan test) -> if orphaned and heavily corrupted, rewrite from scratch preserving logic; if referenced, de-indent carefully
solution: generate_docstrings.py: full rewrite to module-level functions. consistency_checker.py: flagged as orphaned dead code, not rewritten
verification: rewritten file imports clean and logic preserved
generalization: Structural corruption is the most expensive error class — de-indenting by hand is error-prone. First test whether the file is orphaned (grep for references); if dead, rewrite or delete rather than repair. If live, the logic body is usually intact and only indentation needs resetting.

problem: pyflakes flags 12 undefined names in scripts/graphify_huge_mode.py
evidence: file contains ONLY a function body — no imports, no module docstring
graphify_node_limit_patch.py reads this file as text and injects it into the installed graphifyy exporters/html.py
host html.py has ALL the names (verified: nx, json, Path, _html, COMMUNITY_COLORS, sanitize_label, write_text_atomic)
hypotheses: 1. Real broken file
2. Fragment whose environment (host module) provides the names
decision_procedure: Read how the file is consumed (is it imported, or read as text?) -> if read as text and injected, check the HOST defines every flagged name -> verify injection applied in installed package
solution: No change needed — verified false positive. Names come from graphify.exporters.html host module
verification: grep host html.py: all names defined; _write_huge_html present
generalization: Before fixing undefined names, ALWAYS check if the file is a fragment/snippet injected elsewhere. Text-injected fragments are never standalone modules. The consumer (patch script) is the source of truth for what names are legal.

evidence: line 136 is inside if __name__ == '__main__'
KALIWORMS.py builds classes dynamically: globals()[_name] = _make(...) for _name in _TOOLS
NmapWorm is in the _TOOLS list
hypotheses: 1. Real missing class
2. Dynamically created class invisible to static analysis
decision_procedure: Check if the name is produced by globals()/setattr in a loop -> if yes, static tools cannot see it; runtime works fine
verification: runtime creates the class via the loop
generalization: Dynamic class factories (globals()[name] = make(name)) are invisible to static analyzers. Pattern: when pyflakes flags a name that matches a factory loop's string list, it is a false positive.

problem: How to prove a fix worked (not just that it compiled)
evidence: py_compile catches syntax only
pyflakes catches undefined names but flags false positives
import test catches missing deps at module load
hypotheses: Single verification is enough vs layered verification
decision_procedure: Layered protocol: 1) py_compile all 648 files (syntax) 2) pyflakes undefined-name filter with known-false-positive exclusion list 3) smoke import of each fixed critical module 4) run the project's own test suite for touched subsystems 5) for annotation bugs, AST-check evaluation scope
solution: Ran all 5 layers: 648 compile clean, 0 real undefined names, 7 core modules import OK, 48/48 tests pass
verification: Cross-confirmed: import test proves module loads; tests prove behavior; pyflakes proves no remaining undefined references
generalization: A fix is only verified when it passes at least: syntax + reference + import + behavior. The false-positive exclusion list must be re-derived each scan (fragments and dynamic factories change).

note: These 10 reasoning traces cover the 38 fixes (multiple files per class: TR-03 covers 11 files, TR-02 covers 12 files, TR-01 covers 5 blocks). The pattern library is the compressible knowledge; file lists are the instances.
